title: Persistent work claims, expiry and delayed acknowledgement
source_note: Authored development fixture using Python standard-library SQLite transactions and explicit logical time; not an external benchmark or held-out production incident.

defect_notes.incident: Acknowledgement omits claim generation, so an older receipt can complete a newer claim when the worker name is reused.
defect_notes.normal: Reference implementation checks receipt generation and lease expiry using an atomic SQLite update; claim selection/update is within BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
defect_notes.local: Lease expiry truncates the requested duration to an integer, violating fractional timing. This is a scalar calculation defect rather than a handoff ownership defect.

acceptance_limits: The concurrent check uses two independent connections and a synchronized start; this finite schedule does not prove every possible SQLite interleaving.
No wall-clock timing, untrusted fabricated receipts, crash durability, process termination, database lock timeouts, or payload types outside the stated domain are claimed.
Returned receipt dictionaries are treated as opaque: tests pass issued receipts unchanged.
